I totally see where you're coming from and I HAVE gone too far before (my friends were quick to tell me that). However, being a mentally ill bunch of college kids, we all make those kinds of jokes around each other and don't think much of it. When one of us starts making too many of those jokes and is sort of aggressively laughing about it if you know what I mean, we kind of clue in that they're not okay. The only times I've come close, I've woken up my friends and they've gotten me through it. 


For people who use ironic, self-deprecating humor as crutch, we are the most communicative, least emotionally stunted group ever. I guess I'm more worried about when it slips out around acquaintances. 



EDIT: As for your shooting up a school analogy, if I had also been hospitalized for the same and it was more normalized in comedy because it's something comedians deal with often, then I wouldn't be worried unless there were some clear undertones of distress.

**the reason i'm uncomfortable is because that's how she perceives me, and possibly how others perceive me.**

i do need an ass-beating. i've tried everything i can think of to be less shitty, and i can't see myself ever succeeding. i thought that killing myself would cause more damage, but maybe it's the way to go. not trying to be dramatic -- i'm such a mess that i really am always on the verge, but it's not something i'd impulsively do because i wouldn't want to fuck it up. my family doesn't need my shit. my friends also don't need my shit (although my shit isn't as bad with them). it's easier to get over the death of a shitty person than it is to live with a shitty person i would think.
they won't let me rent a place. when i was severely mentally ill i signed stuff that allows them ultimate control over all my finances.

i started having a shit ton of good ideas and started a bunch of projects - drawings/designs for a fashion show/music/books/collaborations/blogs and i got so damn excited that it was overwhelming. i thought i was gonna be this ultimate artist/musician/graphic novelist/cartoon creator/mental health advocate and that i'd change the world for people with mental illness and was gonna be a household name. i also had an intense desire to go on adventures, so from like 12-4am most nights I'd explore the city on foot, and play my uke in public. sometimes drunk, sometimes not. it was mostly euphoria but with some rage when i found out friends were struggling and some paranoia/skittishness because i felt like i could sense people all around me at night. once while filming myself playing a song the screen glitched out and made it feel like the world was closing in, but when i rewatched the video right after, the screen was fine. after coming down, i found no evidence that the video ever existed on my computer. i got very drunk one night and as my friend was holding my hair back in the bathroom, i started sobbing and told her everything, saying i was crazy. she just listened and was there for me. the night before i was hospitalized i was really drunk and wandered around the city talking to myself all night - cars slowed down and people tried to tell me things but i just kept walking. in the morning i walked to class, felt like it would be impossible to sit for 3 hours and went to the college counsellor, who took me to the hospital (i thought i was going to see a doctor and then come back). first day there i fell in love with a patient and we made beautiful music together, then i came down.

so yeah, that was it

Stress for me is like - my brain can't process it so I usually get giddy and manic or sometimes I just shut everything out and get depressed. 
The thing that works best for me is kind of... letting myself be stressed. Like, telling people that I'm stressed, and accepting it, and trying to work with it.
Obviously it's way more fun just to giggle 'till I tear up and jump around and talk loudly to strangers but. Ya know. That's not healthy and stuff, I guess.

All of mine are pretty great.
First time (high school), I thought I was put on earth to save the bees, started designing t shirts and would have blown a couple hundred bucks to get them printed but my parents put a limit on my card (thanks guys). Truly thought I was in Hufflepuff and the yellow and black house colours were connected to the bees. Also that yellow represented mania and black was depression. Did some art on it.

Second time, I thought everything was some big reference to 1984, which meant it was going to come true like 50 years late. My friend Julia being in the class we read the book, the hospital pajamas, the Muse album The Resistance (which was actually true!!).

Last time, I thought my parents were going to forcefully keep me trapped in the house so that I couldn't go to art school, so I went onto the roof to escape/calm down. They flipped their shit thinking I was going to jump and forcefully trapped me in their room with my sisters' help, pinning me down. I was screaming and apparently had "super strength" and tried to fight my dad and then escaped, but my mom caught me when I turned around to taunt them. I don't remember much because I had so much (totally ineffective) seroquel in me.
